title: LLM Prompt Evaluation for Educational Applications
venue: EDM-AIED 2025 Workshop on Epistemics and Decision-Making in AI-Supported Education (co-located with AIED 2025)
extended_summary:
This paper addresses the problem of how to systematically design and evaluate large language model (LLM) prompts for educational applications, rather than relying on ad-hoc prompt engineering. The authors focus on a structured dialogue activity used in an intelligent text web application and ask what a tournament-style prompt evaluation process can reveal about the performance of different prompting strategies for generating pedagogically appropriate follow-up questions.

The intervention studied is a prompt evaluation framework rather than a student learning intervention in the traditional sense. The authors created six prompt templates for Llama 3, including one baseline and five theory-informed alternatives based on prompt design patterns such as Persona, Context Manager, Cognitive Verifier, and Alternative Approaches. These prompts were used to generate follow-up questions after students answered self-explanation reading training questions. Eight trained judges then compared pairs of generated questions using a comparative judgment tournament implemented in Prodigy and ranked with the Glicko2 rating system across criteria of format, dialogue support, and appropriateness for adult learners.

The population consisted of adult learners whose authentic interactions were drawn from three intelligent text deployments: 93 interactions from Prolific crowd workers reading economics, 17 from university students reading psychology, and 9 from college students reading programming. The educational context was an online intelligent text framework called STAIRS that supports reading comprehension and summary revision. The study itself centered on expert judging of LLM outputs generated from these learner interactions rather than direct measurement of student learning gains.

The main conclusion is that systematic prompt evaluation is feasible and useful for educational technology research. The Strategic Reading Coach template performed best, with estimated win probabilities from 81% to 100% against competing prompts, suggesting that combining Persona and Context Manager patterns was especially effective in this reading comprehension dialogue context. The paper argues that prompt engineering for education should move toward evidence-based, replicable evaluation methods, while noting that findings may not generalize beyond this task and that only one LLM was tested.

identified_tools.name: Llama 3
identified_tools.description: A named large language model used to generate educational dialogue content.
identified_tools.use_case: Used within the STAIRS reading-comprehension dialogue system to generate follow-up questions after learners answered an initial SERT question; six prompt templates for Llama 3 were compared in a tournament-style evaluation.

findings.finding_summary: In a tournament-style comparative judgment evaluation of Llama 3 outputs, the Strategic Reading Coach prompt template was the strongest performer for generating reading-comprehension follow-up questions. It showed estimated pairwise win probabilities ranging from 81% against the Scaffolding Expert to 100% against the Baseline and Comprehension Monitor, based on 213 total preference decisions from eight judges using 120 authentic user interactions across three deployments.
findings.measure: Judge preference for LLM-generated follow-up questions on format, dialogue support, and appropriateness for adult learners

findings.finding_summary: Prompt design materially affected the quality of Llama 3-generated follow-up questions. The Scaffolding Expert ranked second and showed strong pairwise performance (1.00 vs Baseline, 0.96 vs Socratic Guide, 0.91 vs Connection Builder), while Comprehension Monitor and Connection Builder performed relatively poorly, indicating that some prompt-pattern combinations were less effective in this reading dialogue context.
findings.measure: Pairwise comparative judgment rankings of prompt templates for LLM-generated follow-up questions
findings.effect_size: SE win probabilities: 1.00 vs Baseline; 0.96 vs SG; 0.91 vs CB

quality_tier_rationale: This is an empirical evaluation with authentic interactions and structured human judging, but it is not an RCT or QED on student learning outcomes. The main outcomes are annotator preferences about prompt quality rather than direct causal evidence on learner achievement.
impact_tier_rationale: The paper reports clear comparative improvements in judged output quality, but impact on students' academic outcomes is not directly measured. As a result, educational impact is promising but unclear.
